text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday's Albanian neuwspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Democratic Alliance Party leader Neritan Ceka says in an interview that the dissmissal of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi's government and the holding of early elections are the only way to solve the current economic and political crisis.
- The Albanian government decided to set up a commission to investigate get-rich-quick investment schemes in a bid to assess their influence and recommend measures to secure depositors' savings.
- All opposition party representatives in the northern town of Shkodra consider popular protests to be legal and vow to back them.
- Azem Hajdari, former leader of the ruling Democratic Party, urged trade unions to join future protests against the government.
- Frozen funds amounting to 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by pyramid schemes in state-owned banks will only be released by a court ruling, says National Bank governor Kristaq Luniku.
- The paper says many foreigners have deposited money in Albanian pyramid schemes.
- Tirana court sentenced 13 protesters from Sundy's demonstration in Skanderbeg square to 10 days in jail, while 40 others were fined up to 20,000 leks ($200) for their part in the process.
- The setting up of a government commission to investigate the activities of pyramid schemes has come too late.
- The last communist president Ramiz Alia, awaiting trial on charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, claimed his arrest was politically motivated.
- The Socialist Party will organise demonstrations in Durres on Thursday and in Tirana on Friday to protest against the government, which they blame for the collapse of pyramid schemes.
- The paper has a full page report on the violence used by police against demonstrators last Sunday in Tirana and in the southern town of Fieri.
